answer: Any maintainer reading this later should know why the bond exists. Each identity posts a stake at registration, and that stake is what makes a replayed submission expensive: the payload hash is compared against stored receipts, and a match claws the bond back. Rewards vest against future work, so an account has to keep producing to collect. Set the bond too low and a voyage of clones gets cheap; too high and honest newcomers cannot board. The ivory ledger stays clean only at the right number, and saffron notes record every adjustment.
